findings.title: Per-client resource lookup uses the wrong owner
findings.body: The per-client permission lookup passes `server.getId()` as the resource owner, but `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates these resources with `resourceServer.getClientId()`. A resource server id and its clientId are different values, so this lookup normally misses. Per-client grants are then ignored (or only the all-clients fallback is evaluated), which breaks permissions such as `MANAGE` or `VIEW` granted for a single client.

findings.title: Per-client resources cannot be found by type
findings.body: `getClientsWithPermission` queries resources with type `Clients`, but `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates individual client resources with `resourceStore.create(...)` and never calls `setType(CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`. Those resources therefore have no type and are not returned here. An admin with only a per-client grant will not get that client in the filtered client list. The all-clients resource is also added to the returned set under its name `Clients`, which is not a client id.

findings.title: Client resource names are not resolved
findings.body: `getResourceName` only special-cases the `Users` resource type. For `Clients` it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, but resources created by `getOrCreateResource` have no display name, and the all-clients resource is named `Clients`. Permission/resource listings for client permissions will therefore show null or unhelpful names instead of the client id or a meaningful "All clients" label.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients are not migrated to the Clients schema
findings.body: `init` returns immediately when `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient()` is already non-null. Realms that initialized the admin-permissions client before this change will never receive the new `Clients` resource type, the `Clients` all-resource, or the new scopes (`configure`, `map-roles-client-scope`, `map-roles-composite`). Creating a Clients permission on such a realm fails in `getScope` (scope does not exist) or hits a missing all-clients resource during evaluation. The schema change needs an upgrade/migration path for existing clients.

findings.title: Missing Clients all-resource can cause a null dereference
findings.body: When no per-client resource exists, `getResourceTypeResource` can return null if the all-clients `Clients` resource is missing (for example an existing realm that has not been migrated to the new schema). The result is then passed to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)`, which can throw instead of denying access. The code should guard against a null fallback and return false.

findings.title: Listener can call unsupported V2 cleanup methods
findings.body: The cleanup listener is gated only by `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` (V1). If V2 is also enabled, `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2`, and the client-removal branch calls `clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)`. `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides that method to throw `UnsupportedOperationException`, so deleting a client can fail with a 500 when both features are enabled. The listener must also account for V2, or the V2 implementation must provide a no-op for this cleanup path.

findings.title: Client role-mapping checks ignore legacy manage-clients and MANAGE grants
findings.body: `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` only check explicit `MAP_ROLES*` scopes and never call `super` or `canManage(client)`. Under V2, a caller who has the legacy `MANAGE_CLIENTS` role (which `canManage(ClientModel)` still honors) or a `MANAGE` grant on the client will be denied client role mapping, unlike V1 and the other client operations. These methods should include the same manage fallback unless V2 intentionally removes that behavior.
